speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our evaluation, how long has this lesion been present and did it start as a blister, bug bite, or open sore?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL)

The patient's history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids and Crohn's disease, combined with a painful ulcerative lesion on her leg, strongly suggests erythema nodosum leprosum, a Type 2 lepra reaction. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to know if the patient has any known history of leprosy (Hansen's disease) or has been exposed to it.
